title: Measures to Close Pay Gap between ITE, Polytechnic and University Graduates
what_it_is: Measures to Close Pay Gap between ITE, Polytechnic and University Graduates

sections.label: Graduate pay gap measures
sections.summary: The Minister was asked about measures to close pay gaps between ITE, polytechnic and university graduates and plans to engage employers on pay disparities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what measures will the Ministry propose to close the pay gap between ITE, polytechnic and university graduates over the course of their careers; and (b) how does the Ministry plan to engage with employers to address pay disparities among graduates in the workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: There are ongoing efforts in partnerships with companies, and we are also working on new initiatives to address the differences in wages.

sections.label: Graduate employment and Work-Study
sections.summary: Over 95% of graduates were employed within six months, and ITE is growing its Work-Study Diploma Programme to 1,500 places yearly by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: More than 95% of graduates were employed within six months after completion of the programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For example, ITE is growing its Work-Study Diploma Programme from 1,200 places to 1,500 places each year by 2025, so more graduates can benefit from Work-Study Programmes.

sections.label: CCP graduate job moves
sections.summary: Over 12,000 polytechnic and ITE graduates benefited from CCPs in the last five years, moving into sectors including air transport, financial services and early childhood.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: More than 12,000 Polytechnic and ITE graduates have benefited from CCPs in the last five years and moved into new jobs into sectors including air transport, financial services and early childhood.

sections.label: Graduate employment tracer surveys
sections.summary: Government tracks graduate employment via surveys, MOE pilots tracer surveys on employment and wages five years after graduation, and Forward Singapore looks at career health.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The Government tracks the employment outcomes of graduates through surveys.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: To complement these surveys, the MOE is working with the IHLs to pilot tracer surveys that can track key trends on graduates' employment status and wages five years after graduation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The findings will then be used to engage the relevant stakeholders to improve employment outcomes for all of graduates.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In response to the Member's suggestion, on top of these surveys and the studies that have been ongoing, as I have said earlier on, it takes all the different stakeholders in our society to come together to recognise the contributions of each and every one of our workers, irrespective of the qualifications.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So broadly, if I may share a bit under the Forward Singapore "Empower" pillar, we are further looking into how to help our workers develop their career health, by helping them to make clearer and informed career decisions; help them to better navigate the labour market as well as be rewarded for their skills.
